strings.XIK_Zhang_Zhihe_hog_desc:
Director of the Department of Internal Affairs
Chinese Communist Party - Liu Shaoqi Leaning
--------------
Born ?th August 1894, Linqiong, Qionglai County, Sichuan Province 

Originally a Sichuan commander, Zhang Zhihe was one of the first Sichuanese to adhere to the Revolution promised by the Communist Party, and has since then remained as the most important radical left political figure in greater Sichuan. He was the representative chosen by Liu to formally proclaim allegiance to the National Revolution in Wuhan, the one who created the 24th, and the defender of Changsha. But out of all historical events he'd experienced, the time he spent in Yan'an with Comrade Mao left him most memories.

Angered by Liu Wenhui's decision to expel the United Front, he left with the Communists for Golmud, but the intensifying factionalism eventually drove him back in 1954, with a renewed goal - To persuade Liu Wenhui to the side of the proletariat, and to continue the Revolution in Xikang and Sichuan. With western China falling into negligence and chaos, Xikang remained the only politically stable area, something Zhang Zhihe has been taking advantage of to further his objectives.
strings.XIK_Xue_Yue_for_desc:
Director of the Secretariat
Kuomintang - Independent Xikang Conservatives
--------------
Born 27th December 1896, Lechang County, Shaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong Province 

The Second Sino-Japanese War was one of humiliation and desperation. Too many good men died because of incompetent leadership and lack of good equipment. Amidst the mediocre military leadership of NRA, however, Xue Yue is one of the few to be feared even by the Japanese. Under his command, the 5th Military Region dealt uncountable casualties to the IJA in southern China, a feat that proved crucial to providing the Nationalist regime safe passage to Chongqing after the fall of Shanxi and the Communists in 1942-1943.

Although a legendary figure, Xue Yue despised the politicking of the Republic he fought for, especially over the long-running despotism of Chiang Kai-shek and his son Ching-kuo, choosing to rather side with Liu Wenhui than endure the chaos in Qinghai. Building a pragmatic, united Kuomintang in Xikang, Xue Yue would rather see it entirely disbanded or renamed than to fall under the grasp of the Chiang dynasty once more.
strings.XIK_Li_Xianchun_eco_desc:
Director of the Department of Financial Affairs
Kuomintang - United Front
--------------
Born ?th ? 1886, Anren, Dayi County, Sichuan Province 

Other than serving the government, Li Xianchun is also the chief executive officer of the Kangyu Corporation, the largest financial conglomerate in Xikang, and the chief director of the Xikang Provincial Bank, cementing his position as the financial Godfather of millions. Li Xianchun is critical in contributing to the developing economy of Xikang, his investments granted tens of thousands of jobs and foo security. However, his efforts would have been impossible, had Li not already possessed booming businesses in Sichuan too. Li Xianchun, alongside his brother Li Guangpu, are the masters of Ya'an and Chengdu, linking the two halves of Sichuan ever since the fall of Chongqing.
strings.XIK_Zhang_Weijiong_sec_desc:
Director of the Department of Security
Nonpartisan
--------------
Born ?th August 1888, Dechang County, Sichuan Province 

Before Zhang Zhihe and Xue Yue's arrival, Zhang Weijiong has always acted as the sole leader of the civilian government besides Liu Wenhui himself. Although he has since left the political scene largely since 1954, Zhang took up the position of Director of the Department of Security, continuing his contribution to the stability of Xikang. Under Zhang's guidance, the Xikang government was checked by strong, auditory power he personally supervised, ridding Xikang of the plague of corruption that would have otherwise been disastrous to its infant economy. His manipulation of religious policies also won the support of many, a foundation upon which Liu's ambitious projects may be executed. After 1954, Zhang Weijiong sided with neither the Nationalists nor the Communists, instead of taking a nonpartisan position as an apolitical strongman that defends Xikang from evil within or without.
strings.XIK_tongqu_of_two_worlds_desc: Xikang is the last Avenue of trade and communication between the two increasingly alienating Chinas, whilst Xikang benefits from it, acquiring goods otherwise unable to manufacture. Under Liu's careful management, Xikang benefitted greatly as a middleman from the quasi international trading, and the two worlds, ever hostile, maintained a grey trading partnership that neither side are willing to admit. All of this is constantly helping build up Ya'an from an irrelevant town to a true regional hub of trade.
strings.XIK_new_xikang_desc: It has been more than two decades since Xikang was made a province, and from then much has changed in the once poor and unenlightened mountains. Emerging as a model province, Xikang's economy gradually transformed into a modern economy following Miao Yuntai's monopoly on drugs that forced local farmers to seek other cash crops. Industrialisation and electrification of Ya'an and Xichang followed quickly, and with physical wealth comes that of the mind. Democracy and the concept of the rights of man are no longer abstract ideas, and all political forces in Xikang knew it would take more than just empty promises to satisfy the demands of the Chinese people.
strings.XIK_24th_army_nra_desc: The Xikang Province remains a military junta, even when taking account of its surprising leniency on the opposition. Xue Yue and Zhang Zhihe may have household troops of their own alongside the 74th, but the 24th Army remains as the chief leader of Xikang politics. As of now, neither Kuomintang nor the Communists pose more threat than the Weimin Society, Chairman Liu's own political party. If Liu Wenhui completely sidelines the 24th, it might as well as shift from the defender of Xikang to its biggest threat.
strings.XIK_panchen_lama_in_exile_desc: The 9th Panchen Lama's presence in Ya'an was highly troublesome, even in his death prior to reincarnation. The guards of Panchen Lama and the minority attempted a coup on the 24th Army, but were soon put down. Immediately after the 10th Panchen Lama's ascension in Yushu, he was expelled by the Tibetan army, for he was an enemy of the Kashag of Jokhang. Seeking refuge in Xikang, the 10th Panchen Lama is not expecting a swift return to Lhasa any time soon, though his maturity and popularity is also beginning to stir trouble as his previous corporeal form did.
strings.XIK_restless_elite_desc: Before even the foundation of Xikang, the minority elite of Xikang, who had deep connections with Chiang Kai-shek attempted to subvert Liu's rule through the so-called Kang Self-Governance Movement. Though the elite has lost their influence since the Garze Incident under the lead of Liu Jiaju, since the foundation of the binary regime Golmud has been ever forging a stronger bond with Ya'an. And those who thought their time was over became once more agitated, especially in the Kang regions, a notion that must not develop unchecked.
strings.XIK_costs_of_peace_desc: Liu Wenhui was never an easily satiated man. Though the mountains of Xikang are flowing with gold, his ambition reaches far higher than even their highest peaks. The sole purpose of developing Xikang was, is, and will always be retaking the Sichuan basin, as he rightfully deserves. Though Chairman Liu knows his men can easily best the Sichuanese, it is no longer merely an issue of China. Long has the possibility of a Japanese intervention haunted him. Liu Wenhui might emerge as a great man of Sichuan and potentially the entirety of China, but for now, Liu wouldn't be returning to Chengdu anytime soon.
